title: Release Triangle Matrix & Scope Fidelity Plan for API / Console / Runtime
creator: Ariana Chen
description: Establish a compact decision framework (the 'Release Triangle') that trades off scope fidelity, reliability risk, and GTM readiness across API, Console and Runtime workstreams. Produce explicit cut criteria, staging windows, a rollout heatmap, and a communications cadence so that engineering, design, support, and growth teams can make deterministic go/no-go decisions during the release train.
milestones: M1: Feature freeze for Fidelity Tier A (API + Runtime core) - 2026-03-10
M2: Staging window 1: end-to-end regression and perf gates - 2026-03-17
M5: Scoped GA if metrics pass (rolling to 100%) - 2026-03-28
scope_fidelity_tiers: Tier A: Core API surface & runtime kernel changes required for SLA. Must be in this train or deferred.
Tier B: Console UX improvements and observability panels. Include if stability metrics are green after staging window.
Tier C: Nice-to-have features, promo copy, and extended examples. Auto-deferred to next train unless explicit approval is granted.
cut_criteria: Latency SLO: p95 token latency increase <= 10% vs baseline over a 1h window in staging
Error budget: no sustained 5xx > 0.3% over 30m across canary hosts
Regression: No severity 1 functional regressions in core inference paths
Observability: Dashboard coverage for new metrics and alerts created and reviewed
Docs: Release notes draft and console help copy reviewed by Docs and Legal
rollout_heatmap: Green: All metrics within cut criteria -> proceed with canary expansion
Yellow: One non-critical metric outside threshold -> hold and run hotfix window (2 business days)
Red: Any SLO breach or functional regression -> rollback to previous model/runtime version and escalate
decisions: Use canary percentage progression of 0% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 1h observation windows between steps for latency-sensitive customers
Conservative default: defer all Tier C items unless PM signs off after M2
Adopt existing runtime fallback policy (model-variant fallback) as primary safety mechanism during rollout
open_risks: KV cache regressions under long-context workloads could silently increase tail latency
Dependency: GPU kernel patch (ENG-4921) must land and pass perf tests before M2
Documentation lag: growth assets and release notes may not be ready by M3 if writer headcount is limited
acceptance_criteria: All Tier A features either feature-flagged or merged behind experiments with owners assigned
M2 perf/regression gates executed with artifacts and signoff from eng lead
Release notes published to the docs site and release channel, with changelog entries for API changes
At least one dry-run rollback executed in staging and documented runbook updated
